title: Which overlapping coin pattern appears first?
problem: A fair coin is tossed independently until either HHTHTTHH or HTHHHTTH first appears as a consecutive block. What is the exact probability that HHTHTTHH appears first? H denotes heads and T denotes tails. Overlapping occurrences count; do not restart the search after partial matches.
solution:
Write A = HHTHTTHH and B = HTHHHTTH. Track the longest suffix of the toss history that is a proper prefix of A or B. This retains every partial match, including overlapping ones. Let p(s) be the probability that A wins starting from state s, and set p(A)=1 and p(B)=0. For each nonterminal state, independence and fairness give p(s)=(p(next(s,H))+p(next(s,T)))/2. The transitions and exact values are:

empty: H -> H, T -> empty; p = 64/129
H: H -> HH, T -> HT; p = 64/129
HH: H -> HH, T -> HHT; p = 65/129
HT: H -> HTH, T -> empty; p = 21/43
HHT: H -> HHTH, T -> empty; p = 65/129
HTH: H -> HTHH, T -> HT; p = 62/129
HHTH: H -> HTHH, T -> HHTHT; p = 22/43
HTHH: H -> HTHHH, T -> HHT; p = 61/129
HHTHT: H -> HTH, T -> HHTHTT; p = 71/129
HTHHH: H -> HH, T -> HTHHHT; p = 19/43
HHTHTT: H -> HHTHTTH, T -> empty; p = 80/129
HTHHHT: H -> HHTH, T -> HTHHHTT; p = 49/129
HHTHTTH: H -> HHTHTTHH, T -> HT; p = 32/43
HTHHHTT: H -> HTHHHTTH, T -> empty; p = 32/129

Each displayed value satisfies its transition equation by exact substitution. These equations have a unique bounded solution: in each disjoint block of eight future tosses there is probability at least 1/256 of seeing A and hence stopping (if not stopped earlier). Thus survival through k such blocks has probability at most (255/256)^k, which tends to zero. Iterating the averaging equations shows that any difference between two bounded solutions with the same terminal values is at most its initial maximum times this survival probability; therefore the difference is zero. The initial state is empty, giving the stated probability. The patterns have equal length and differ, so they cannot first finish on the same toss.
